newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Koor plans Gulf road show.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Koor plans Gulf road show.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries plans to send a delegation on an investors road show to a Gulf state later this year, Koor President Benjamin Gaon was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"I can't go into details because I don't want to destroy the plan," The Jerusalem Post quoted Gaon as telling a meeting of the newspaper's senior staff on Monday. "It's enough of a statement that it's kosher; it means it's not a secret."
Gaon, head of Israel's largest industrial concern, declined to name the Gulf country or say when the road show would take place, the newspaper said.
Oman and Qatar have raced ahead of other Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel but have stopped short of forging full diplomatic relations.

"Being an Israeli entrepreneur and an Israeli businessman is no longer a liability, in fact it has become an asset worldwide. I don't have to apologise that I am an Israeli or to hide my identity," he was quoted as saying.
Gaon cited an expanding circle of countries where Israel now does business, mentioning Indonesia, India, China and Japan, the newspaper said.

Asked about the recent purchase of a stake in Koor by Egyptian businessman Ibrahim Kamel, chairman of the Kato group of companies, Gaon was quoted as saying he "had no idea" of the size of the holding.
Kamel visited Israel last month as Gaon's guest and met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"I insisted that if he came to Israel he would do so in the wide open, in the full limelight of the media," Gaon was quoted as saying.
